sources.title: Original T5 release README
sources.evidence: October 23 repository state explicitly lists T5-Base, nominal 220M, and links the released original base checkpoint. The README describes text-to-text tasks, transfer learning and a default 512-token training sequence length. Freshly reopened the original pinned raw README October 27; it still explicitly names the original Base checkpoint and nominal 220M total.

sources.title: Original release commit metadata
sources.evidence: Release-containing commit authored 2019-10-23T23:34:41Z and committed 2019-10-23T23:52:05Z. Combined with the same-day public paper and checkpoint links, supports the October 23 release rather than the later February 2020 blog.

sources.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
sources.evidence: First submitted October 23, 2019; current revision September 2023. Paper describes a dense encoder-decoder Transformer, with base dimensions 12 encoder/12 decoder blocks, width 768, 12 heads, head width 64 and feed-forward width 3072. Relative attention uses 32 learned scalar buckets shared across layers within each stack. Training uses length 512; this is not a demonstrated architectural maximum.

sources.title: Original T5-base operative configuration
sources.evidence: Exact original base checkpoint: 12 layers per stack, width 768, FFN 3072, 12 heads and key/value width 64. Inputs and targets length 512, all_mix training with denoising, shared encoder/decoder embeddings and tied decoder softmax. Vocabulary padded to a divisor of 128; this is the original stored shape, not added HF conversion rows. Fresh October 27 retrieval reconfirmed these dimensions and the original checkpoint path; no tensor index or weights were downloaded in this pass.

sources.title: Original T5-base TensorFlow checkpoint index
sources.evidence: Read only the 11,385-byte index. Independently parsed SSTable/Snappy and TensorFlow BundleEntryProto shapes: 257 BF16 model tensors totaling 222,903,552 elements after excluding optimizer slots and global_step. Every included tensor has unsliced storage and byte size equal to two times shape product. Encoder weights 84,954,240; decoder 113,275,008; shared embedding 24,674,304. Two self-attention relative-bias tables total 768; normalization scales total 47,616. There is no cross-attention relative-bias tensor in the original model. No weight payload downloaded.

sources.title: Exact converted T5-base configuration
sources.evidence: T5ForConditionalGeneration with the same 12-layer base dimensions and vocabulary 32128. It records n_positions=512, but the T5 attention implementation uses relative position buckets, not a fixed absolute-position table or a 512-position bound.

sources.title: Converted T5-base tensor header
sources.evidence: HTTP 206 ranges 0-7 and 8-30645 retrieved only the 30,638-byte JSON header. It lists 258 F32 tensors totaling 222,903,936 elements. This is 384 above the original count because it includes decoder.block.0.layer.1.EncDecAttention.relative_attention_bias.weight, explicitly ignored by current Transformers. One shared 32128-by-768 embedding is stored; no duplicated encoder/decoder/lm_head embedding or quantization-scale metadata is present.

sources.title: Pinned Transformers T5 implementation
sources.evidence: T5ForConditionalGeneration ties encoder, decoder and lm_head embeddings to shared.weight. Cross-attention instantiates no relative bias and explicitly ignores the legacy extra bias on load. The only learned relative bias tables are the first encoder and decoder self-attention tables. Dynamic relative offsets are bucketed without a fixed sequence-length ceiling; dense attention, ReLU FFNs and normalization scales account for the remaining original tensors.

sources.title: T5 Base model card
sources.evidence: Card written by Hugging Face identifies original T5-Base, nominal 220M, Apache 2.0, text-to-text use and original mixed unsupervised/supervised training. It does not advertise a dedicated thinking mode or tool-calling interface. This is not T5-v1.1 or Flan-T5. Freshly reopened the complete pinned raw card October 27; its total remains nominal 220M and it supplies no separate active count.

sources.title: Original T5 Apache2.0 license
sources.evidence: Original release repository provides Apache License 2.0; the converted checkpoint card also declares Apache 2.0.

sources.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners, Appendix D
sources.evidence: Later research Table D.1 includes T5-Base nominal 220M and a one-half active fraction for a simplified training-FLOP estimate, explicitly ignoring attention. This approximation is not a developer-defined per-token inference active count and is not promoted to the catalog active parameter field.

sources.title: TensorFlow checkpoint index schema
sources.evidence: BundleEntryProto maps fields 1/2/5 to dtype, tensor shape and storage bytes, with field 7 denoting slices. The original base index has no sliced model tensors. The companion DataType schema identifies 14 as BF16, validating the index-only shape accounting.

sources.title: Merge, Then Compress: Demystify Efficient SMoE with Hints from Its Routing Policy
sources.evidence: Freshly read the original paper and visually inspected Table 1 on page 6. Its caption defines act-size as activated parameters for each token; the exact t5-base dense baseline row gives 220M act-size and 220M total. Section 4.1 describes their baseline fine-tuning/evaluation. This is the authors’ nominal comparison convention, not an exact phase-resolved tensor measurement or a new Google disclosure.

sources.title: MC-SMoE original T5 baseline implementation
sources.evidence: Freshly retrieved the pinned implementation linked by the ICLR paper. Lines 83–84 load T5ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained("t5-base") and its tokenizer. Establishes the original T5 Base checkpoint identity, not Flan-T5 or the pruned/merged Switch model. No model weights were loaded or downloaded.

sources.title: Entities as Experts: Sparse Memory Access with Entity Supervision
sources.evidence: Freshly read full original paper. Table 3 identifies T5-Base at nominal 220M under a total-parameter column; Appendix A identifies T5 and its task fine-tuning. It does not give a Base activated-count row. Its original results support exact baseline identity but do not themselves supply the accepted active value.

sources.title: Entities: what are they, where are they and how do we model them?
sources.evidence: Freshly opened the original TAC keynote. Slide 74 explicitly separates All and Activated counts for T5 3B and 11B, but does not list Base. Those sibling counts are not transferred to Base.

sources.title: SPARSEFIT: Few-shot Prompting with Sparse Fine-tuning for Jointly Generating Predictions and Natural Language Explanations
sources.evidence: Freshly read the original paper after an active-parameters search hit. Section 3 and Appendix A use active for trainable subsets while all other parameters are frozen. This does not establish inference-time participation; its component percentages are not used for the catalog active count.

sources.title: Mixture of Experts Architecture for Machine Translation on Edge Devices
sources.evidence: Freshly read the complete original Tibetan-translation experiment report. Its resource table claims Base 220M active/token, but gives no parameter-count source/method and justifies it with dense-equals-all prose; its FLOPs-per-token units are unexplained. Its measured translation scores are primary results, but the unsupported resource table is not the basis of the accepted count.

sources.title: Flan-T5 Base developer configuration
sources.evidence: Fresh configuration has gated-GELU FFNs of width 2048 and untied word embeddings, unlike original Base’s ReLU width 3072 and shared/tied embeddings. A Flan-T5 active count cannot transfer through an unchanged-architecture assumption.

sources.title: MTEB Flan-T5 Base profile
sources.evidence: Freshly opened numeric lead listing 248M total and 223M active. It identifies google/flan-t5-base, a structurally distinct later model. Its active figure is not used for original T5 Base.

name.note: Normalize display capitalization to the official T5-Base name; original model, not Flan or v1.1.

developer.note: Original Google Research model; authors and release repository establish the developer.

release_date.note: Original release-containing repository commit and initial paper agree on October 23. Later HF conversion uploads and February 2020 blog are not the original release.

open_weights.note: Original checkpoint is linked publicly and its metadata is accessible; converted complete weights are also publicly distributed.

license.note: Supported by original release license and exact converted model card.

parameters_b.note: Exact complete original parameter count: 222,903,552. Sum encoder 84,954,240 + decoder 113,275,008 + shared embedding 24,674,304, counting tied embedding/output once. Includes 62 norm vectors (47,616 elements) and two relative-bias tables (768 elements). Independent base-dimension formula matches original index. Excludes optimizer slots/global_step and the HF-only unused 384-element cross-attention bias. Original BF16 and converted F32 are unpacked floating-point tensors; no quantization metadata is counted. Nominal 220M is rounded. October 27 re-audit freshly confirms the published nominal 220M total and original checkpoint identity through release README, operative config and pinned card. Retain the earlier independently established exact total without repeating its tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 220M under Li et al.’s original ICLR 2024 MC-SMoE comparison convention. Table 1 explicitly defines act-size as activated parameters per token and lists t5-base at 220M. The linked pinned code loads the original t5-base model, establishing exact identity rather than a compressed Switch or Flan variant. This is the research authors’ published nominal convention, not the exact 222,903,552 checkpoint total or a measurement separately resolving encoder processing and cached decoding. Fresh exact-model total/active/activated and later-comparison searches also checked original release/config/card, the full T5 paper, EaE, Bikel’s slides, SPARSEFIT, OpenPecha and the Flan lead. GPT-3’s half-active training-FLOP approximation, trainable-only percentages, sibling counts and structurally different Flan counts are not substituted.

architecture.note: Dense encoder-decoder Transformer, twelve blocks per stack, ReLU feed-forward layers and relative attention biases. No routed experts; not decoder-only and not the gated-GELU v1.1 variant.

context_window.note: 512 is the original training/default input and target length, also stored as legacy n_positions. Relative attention has no fixed absolute-position table or code-enforced 512 ceiling. No single maximum context length is established, and arbitrary-length quality is not claimed.

modalities.note: Original text-to-text model; task labels and target strings are textual, with no image/audio encoder.

reasoning.note: No dedicated thinking mode is documented for the exact original base checkpoint. Benchmark task-solving and textual explanations do not establish the catalog reasoning feature; no unsupported negative inferred.

tool_call.note: No source-reported function/tool-calling capability or explicit negative is documented for original T5-base. A possible downstream fine-tune or wrapper is not evidence about this checkpoint.

description.value: Google’s encoder-decoder T5 model trained on text denoising and supervised text-to-text tasks.
description.note: Plain original-model architecture/training description, distinct from instruction-tuned Flan-T5 and unsupervised-only T5-v1.1.

patch.name: T5 Base
patch.description: Google’s encoder-decoder T5 model trained on text denoising and supervised text-to-text tasks.

sources.label: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

patch.notes: The original checkpoint has 222,903,552 parameters across encoder, decoder and shared embedding; tied input/output weights count once. Nominal 220M active follows Li et al.’s MC-SMoE comparison convention, without separate encoder/decode-phase counts. The unused 384-value HF cross-attention bias is excluded from the total. Training/default length is 512 tokens per input/target, not a fixed maximum. Thinking mode and tool calling remain unverified. Original release: October 23, 2019.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains the verified 222,903,552 original total and recovers nominal 220M active from Li et al.’s original ICLR 2024 MC-SMoE Table 1, with exact original T5 Base identity confirmed in linked baseline code. The count follows that research comparison convention rather than a phase-resolved inference census. Original sources and concrete alternative leads were freshly checked; all twelve unrelated field assessments remain unchanged. No weights or tensor census were downloaded or repeated.
